A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete 29-page v2 and 33-page v3, including Appendices A–D, provide readable text, equations, and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original experiments on Gaussian-mixture data and MNIST, including singular-value spectra, training trajectories, and feature visualizations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain original Gaussian-mixture and MNIST experiments, including results across 100 random initializations.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a fixed first-layer representation and describes W2 as unregularized in Equation 9 and the Theorem 4.2 proof sketch; v2 excludes only W1. However, v3 Equation 12 and the experimental loss still penalize W2. A consistent change to the operative objective or training procedure cannot be established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture classification setting and MNIST experiments. No dataset, domain, task, or distinct input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Both compare trained networks with their own theoretical predictions and across parameter settings. Neither reports evaluated external baseline methods; the expanded citations in v3 do not introduce experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The stated empirical protocols retain the 200-example MNIST sample, network configurations, tanh activations, and regularization coefficients. No revised training or testing procedure is documented. Changes in displayed sweep panels do not establish that the underlying experiments changed.

E4.justification: Parameter-sensitivity evidence is reduced: the additional feedforward sweep in v2 Figure 4 is only partially retained, and the ResNet panels for δ = 2 and δ = 1 disappear from v3 Figure 4. The convergence, Gram-matrix, and projected-feature analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both Section 5.3 and Figure 3 report 100 random initializations, averages, and shading between observed minima and maxima. No new uncertainty estimator, significance test, or repeated-run practice appears.

E6.justification: The spectrum labeled δ = 5 in v2 Figure 4 reappears labeled δ = 10 in v3 Figure 2, without explanation. The original feedforward δ = 10 and δ = 8 spectra and ResNet δ = 2 and δ = 1 panels are omitted. Other matched plots and principal qualitative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 redefines the constrained problem around fixed Z1, changes the layer range and constants of the spectral constraints, and adds analytic non-polynomial activation and generic-backbone conditions. New Remark B.2 and Lemma B.3 address backbone representability. Theorem 4.6 and Remark C.3 generalize the specific first-layer perturbation to a nonnegative lower-semicontinuous function. These materially revise the theoretical setting.

C1.justification: The rank–TCV connection, optimality of DNC1, and absence of loss barriers remain the central contributions. v3 frames optimality more explicitly as a constrained representation-cost result and adds an explicit first-time rigorous-connection claim in Section 1.1.

C2.justification: The new backbone discussion explains how generic full-rank first-layer features make an additional representability constraint automatic, qualifying the applicability of the optimality argument. Interpretations of weight decay, collapse, singular-value convergence, and the large-depth regime are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 Section 5.3 specifies numerical ranks up to 10^-5 relative error; v3 removes this tolerance without supplying a replacement. The NVIDIA A100 80GB hardware disclosure and other experimental implementation details remain.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands the neural-collapse literature discussion across unconstrained-feature models, losses, dynamics, manifold constraints, and graph networks. It explicitly contrasts the work with restrictions of prior Deep-UFM analyses. New references also support the backbone argument, including Chu et al. and Mityagin.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with new contribution and architectural-constraint subsections. Definitions and theoretical discussion are reorganized, proof sketches are inserted into the main text, and the discretization corollary and large-depth discussion move from the appendix into Section 4.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset throughout with different typography, margins, headings, and author layout. Feedforward spectra previously distributed between main text and appendix become a six-panel main figure, the ResNet figure loses two panels, and retained figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: Expanded research positioning, proof sketches, and the generic-backbone lemma improve explanation. However, v3 fixes Z1 in Definition 4.1 while Appendix B.1 still optimizes it, and Equations 9 and 12 disagree about penalizing W2. Figure 2 also reassigns the earlier δ = 5 spectrum to δ = 10 without explanation. These unresolved changes affect central theoretical consistency and result traceability, preventing a reliable judgment of net improvement.
